**Question**

I have $30$ tiles to make a pattern on a grid. The pattern is a series of squares.

![papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/2019/sample-paper-1/s02-q17-s04-i00.png](/assets/papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/2019/sample-paper-1/s02-q17-s04-i00.png "papers/alderley-edge-school-for-girls/2019/sample-paper-1/s02-q17-s04-i00.png")

I have used some of the $30$ tiles to make my pattern.
Do I have enough tiles to make the next square, of side length $4?$
Show working to explain your answer.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I have $30$ tiles to make a pattern on a grid. The pattern is a series of squares.
<emptyline>
%image%
<emptyline>
I have used some of the $30$ tiles to make my pattern.
Do I have enough tiles to make the next square, of side length $4?$
Show working to explain your answer.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Tiles needed}        &= 4 \times 4 \\\\
                            &= 16 \\\\
\text {Tiles used}          &= 1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 \\\\
                            &= 1 + 4 + 9 \\\\
                            &= 14 \\\\
\text {Tiles Left}          &= 30 - 14 \\\\
                            &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

There are enough tiles to make the next square.
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

Yes

**Question**

What fraction of students said “Comedy”?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

<div class="workings">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Fraction}     &= \dfrac {90} {360} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {90} {4 \times 90} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {90}} {4 \times \cancel {90}} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {1} {4}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">

Work out the total number of students that Betty asked.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the total number of students $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {120} {360} \times a     &= 20 \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {20 \times 360} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {20 \times 3 \times 120} {120} \\\\
a                               &= \dfrac {20 \times 3 \times \cancel {120}} {\cancel {120}} \\\\
a                               &= 20 \times 3 \\\\
a                               &= 60
\end{aligned}
$

Total number of students $= 60$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Seven out of forty pupils said they watch the news on television. 
What angle would this be on a pie chart? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Seven out of forty pupils said they watch the news on television. 
What angle would this be on a pie chart? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {Angle}   &= \dfrac {7} {40} \times 360 \\\\
                &= \dfrac {7 \times 360} {40} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {7 \times 9 \times 40} {40} \\\\
                &= \dfrac {7 \times 9 \times \cancel {40}} {\cancel {40}} \\\\
                &= 7 \times 9 \\\\
                &= 63 \degree
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$63 \degree$

</div>
</div>

North beat South in $1999, 2001$ and $2002$.

|   Year    | North        | South        | Difference    |
|:------:   |:--------:    |:--------:    |:----------------------:   |
| $1999$    |   $200$      |    $120$     |      $200 - 120 = 80$     |
| $2001$    |   $150$      |    $130$     |      $150 - 130 = 20$     |
| $2002$    |   $260$      |    $100$     |      $260 - 160 = 100$    |

Year $= 2002$
</div>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

This formula tells you how tall a boy is likely to be when he grows up.

| Add the mother's and father's heights. Divide by $2$. Add $7 \ \text{cm}$ to the result. The boy is likely to be this height, plus or minus $10 \ \text{cm}$. |
|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------:|

Marc's mother is $168\ \text{cm}$ tall. His father is $194\ \text{cm}$ tall.

What is the greatest height Marc is likely to be when he grows up? 

Show your working.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">This formula tells you how tall a boy is likely to be when he grows up.
<emptyline>
| Add the mother's and father's heights. Divide by $2$. Add $7 \ \text{cm}$ to the result. The boy is likely to be this height, plus or minus $10 \ \text{cm}$. |
|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------:|
<emptyline>
Marc's mother is $168\ \text{cm}$ tall. His father is $194\ \text{cm}$ tall.
<emptyline>
What is the greatest height Marc is likely to be when he grows up? 
<emptyline>
Show your working.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Max height of Marc}           &= \dfrac {1} {2} \times (168 + 194) + 7 + 10 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {168 + 194} {2} + 17  \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {362} {2} + 17 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {2 \times 181} {2} + 17 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 181} {\cancel 2} + 17 \\\\
                                    &= 181 + 17 \\\\
                                    &= 198 \ \text{cm}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$191 \ \text{cm}$

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The pie chart has an angle of $90 \degree$ for the Tour de France.

How many people does this represent?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The pie chart has an angle of $90 \degree$ for the Tour de France.
<emptyline>
How many people does this represent?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of people}     &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 80 \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {90 \times 80} {360} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 20} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 20} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                            &= 20
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

| Red | Blue | Green | Yellow | Orange |
|:---:|:----:|:-----:|:------:|:------:|
| $5$ |  $7$ |  $8$  |   $3$  |   $2$  |

A pie chart is drawn to show children's favourite colour using the table above. What size angle would represent Red?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

| $5$ |  $7$ |  $8$  |   $3$  |   $2$  |
<emptyline>

</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Angle red}                            &= \dfrac {5} {5 + 7 + 8 + 3 + 2} \times 360 \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {5} {25} \times 360 \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {5 \times 360} {25} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {5 \times 5 \times 72} {5 \times 5} \\\\
                                            &= \dfrac {\cancel 5 \times \cancel 5 \times 72} {\cancel 5 \times \cancel 5} \\\\
                                            &= 72 \degree
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

$180$ children were surveyed as to their favourite pastime. The results are in the pie chart above. How many children prefer computers?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                                                        &= \dfrac {93 \times \cancel{2} \times \cancel{180}} {\cancel{2} \times \cancel{180}} \\\\
                                                        &= 93
\end{aligned}
$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

                                                &= \dfrac {135} {360} \times 1200 \\\\

                                                &= \dfrac {3 \times 45 \times 120 \times 10} {120 \times 3} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 3 \times 45 \times \cancel {120} \times 10} {\cancel {120} \times \cancel 3} \\\\
                                                &= 45 \times 10 \\\\
                                                &= 450
\end{aligned}
$

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$

\text{Children who liked football}              &= \dfrac {360 - 90 - 45 - 60 - 30} {360} \times 1200 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {360 - 225} {360} \times 1200 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {135} {360} \times 1200 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {135 \times 1200} {360} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {3 \times 45 \times 120 \times 10} {120 \times 3} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 3 \times 45 \times \cancel {120} \times 10} {\cancel {120} \times \cancel 3} \\\\
                                                &= 45 \times 10 \\\\
                                                &= 450
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

Write down the percentage of children who have two siblings.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Write down the percentage of children who have two siblings.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{\% of children with 2 siblings}           &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 100 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {90 \times 100} {360} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 25} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 25} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                                &= 25\%
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                                                &= \dfrac {3} {8}
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

$8$ of the children who were surveyed had one sibling.

Fill in the table below to show the number of children who have $0, 2$ and $3$ siblings.

|      Number of siblings     | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
|:---------------------------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Number of children surveyed |     | $8$ |     |     |

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>

<emptyline>

</code></pre>

**Working**

Let the total number of children surveyed $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac {45} {360} \times a          &= 8 \\\\
a                                   &= 8 \times \dfrac {360} {45} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {8 \times 360} {45} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {8 \times 8 \times 45} {45} \\\\
a                                   &= \dfrac {8 \times 8 \times \cancel {45}} {\cancel {45}} \\\\
a                                   &= 8 \times 8 \\\\
a                                   &= 64
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Children with no siblings}    &= \dfrac {135} {360} \times 64 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {135 \times 64} {360} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {45 \times 3 \times 8 \times 8} {45 \times 8} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {45} \times 3 \times 8 \times \cancel 8} {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 8} \\\\
                                    &= 24 \\\\
\text{Children with 2 siblings}     &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 64 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {90 \times 64} {360} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 16} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 16} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                    &= 16 \\\\
\text{Children with 3 siblings}     &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 64 \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {90 \times 64} {360} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 16} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                    &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 16} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                    &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

|      Number of siblings     | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
|:---------------------------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Number of children surveyed | $24$| $8$ | $16$| $16$|
</div>

**Question**

Peter walked at $4\ \text{km/h}$. 

How far is it around the school field? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Peter walked at $4\ \text{km/h}$. 
<emptyline>
How far is it around the school field? 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR: It is really important to use the right units in calculations and convert where required.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text {Distance} = \text{Speed} \times \text{Time}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Distance}     &= 4 \ \text{km/h} \times \dfrac {15} {60} \ \text{h} \\\\
                    &= 4 \ \text{km/h} \times \dfrac {15} {60} \ \text{h} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 15} {60} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 15} {4 \times 15} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {15}} {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {15}} \\\\
                    &= 1 \ \text{km}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Distance}     &= 4 \ \text{km/h} \times \dfrac {15} {60} \ \text{h} \\\\
                    &= 4 \ \text{km/h} \times \dfrac {15} {60} \ \text{h} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 15} {60} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {4 \times 15} {4 \times 15} \\\\
                    &= \dfrac {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {15}} {\cancel 4 \times \cancel {15}} \\\\
                    &= 1 \ \text{km}
\end{aligned}
$

**Question**

I have $30$ tiles to make a pattern on a grid.

The pattern is a series of squares.

I have used some of the $30$ tiles to make my pattern.

Do I have enough tiles left to make the next square, of side length $4?$

Show working to explain your answer.

![papers/kent-college-canterbury/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q17-s04-i00.png](/assets/papers/kent-college-canterbury/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q17-s04-i00.png "papers/kent-college-canterbury/2020/sample-paper-1/s01-q17-s04-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">I have $30$ tiles to make a pattern on a grid.
<emptyline>
The pattern is a series of squares.
<emptyline>
I have used some of the $30$ tiles to make my pattern.
<emptyline>
Do I have enough tiles left to make the next square, of side length $4?$
<emptyline>
Show working to explain your answer.
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Tiles required}   &= 4 \times 4 \\\\
                        &= 16 \\\\
\text{Tiles used}       &= 1 + 2 \times 2 + 3 \times 3 \\\\
                        &= 1 + 4 + 9 \\\\
                        &= 14 \\\\
\text{Tiles remaining}  &= 30 - 14 \\\\
                        &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
a + a + 24              &= 96 \\\\

2a                      &= 96 - 24 \\\\

a                       &= \dfrac {72} {2} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {2 \times 36} {2} \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac {\cancel 2 \times 36} {\cancel 2} \\\\
a                       &= 36
\end{aligned}
$

Number of games won $= 36$

**Question**

In an attempt to improve the environment children are encouraged to find a “greener” way to get to school. A third of those who travel by car decide to walk and $3$ move from bus to walking too. How many now walk?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">In an attempt to improve the environment children are encouraged to find a “greener” way to get to school. A third of those who travel by car decide to walk and $3$ move from bus to walking too. How many now walk?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of children}           &= 14 + \dfrac {1} {3} \times 15 + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 14 + \dfrac {15} {3} + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 14 + \dfrac {5 \times 3} {3} + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 14 + \dfrac {5 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel 3} + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 14 + 5 + 3 \\\\
                                    &= 22
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$22$

</div>
</div>

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many black cars are there?

<div class="workings">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Black cars}               &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 120 \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {90 \times 120} {360} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {3 \times 30 \times 120} {120 \times 3} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {\cancel 3 \times 30 \times \cancel {120}} {\cancel {120} \times \cancel 3} \\\\
                                &= 30
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

                    &= 60

                                            &= 18

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

                            &= \dfrac {45 \times 64} {360} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {45 \times 8 \times 8} {45 \times 8} \\\\
                            &= \dfrac {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 8 \times 8} {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 8} \\\\
                            &= 8
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

\end{aligned}
$

\end{aligned}

**Question**

What percentage of girls have brown hair?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What percentage of girls have brown hair?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{\% of girl with brown hair}               &= \dfrac {9 + 15} {11 + 15 + 9 + 10 + 5} \times 100 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {24} {50} \times 100 \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {24 \times 100} {50} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {24 \times 50 \times 2} {50} \\\\
                                                &= \dfrac {24 \times \cancel {50} \times 2} {\cancel {50}} \\\\
                                                &= 24 \times 2 \\\\
                                                &= 48 \%
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$48 \%$

</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {45} \times 3 \times \cancel 8 \times 3} {\cancel {45} \times \cancel 8} \\\\
                        &= 3 \times 3 \\\\
                        &= 9
\end{aligned}

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-2/s01-q30-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-2/s01-q30-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2015/group-2/s01-q30-i00.png")

**Question**

Charlotte removes a third of the woodlice from pot $B$ and $20\%$ of the woodlice from pot $C$. 
She puts these woodlice under a new pot, $F$.

How many woodlice are under pot $F$?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Charlotte removes a third of the woodlice from pot $B$ and $20\%$ of the woodlice from pot $C$. 
She puts these woodlice under a new pot, $F$.
<emptyline>
How many woodlice are under pot $F$?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Woodlice under pot F}             &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times 4.5 \times 2 + 20 \% \times 5 \times 2  \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {1} {3} \times 9 + \dfrac {20} {100} \times 10  \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {9} {3} + \dfrac {20 \times 10} {100} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {3 \times 3} {3} + \dfrac {20 \times 10} {100} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {3 \times \cancel 3} {\cancel 3} + \dfrac {2 \cancel 0 \times 1 \cancel 0} {1 \cancel 0 \cancel 0} \\\\
                                        &= 3 + 2 \\\\
                                        &= 5
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$5$

</div>

**Question**

**Estimate** the amount of Brie sold by Tosco in $1 \ \text{week}$.

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">**Estimate** the amount of Brie sold by Tosco in $1 \ \text{week}$.
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Brie sold by Tosco}               &= \dfrac {90} {360} \times 300 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {90 \times 300} {360} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {90 \times 4 \times 75} {90 \times 4} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4 \times 75} {\cancel {90} \times \cancel 4} \\\\
                                        &= 75 \ \text{kg}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$75 \ \text{kg}$

What is the average (mean) number of pizzas sold per day?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<div class="formulas" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
- ABBR: $\text{Mean} = \dfrac {\text{Total of items}} {\text{Number of items}}$
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Average number of pizzas} &= \dfrac {15 + 13 + 8 + 10 + 5 + 9} {6} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {60} {6} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {10 \times 6} {6} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac {10 \times \cancel 6} {\cancel 6} \\\\
                                &= 10
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
